description: Compare each patient's average GOT with the mean of the per-patient averages.

a.request: For each patient in `Laboratory` (grouped by `ID`), give the patient ID, their average GOT, their average RBC, and their average GOT minus the mean of all patients' average GOT values. That single overall figure is used for every patient, and if it is missing, return no rows. Ignore missing values in all averages. Show the 10 patients with the largest difference, highest first with missing differences last, unrounded.
a.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(GOT) AS avg_got, AVG(RBC) AS avg_rbc
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
), overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_got) AS mean_avg_got
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT p.ID, p.avg_got, p.avg_rbc, p.avg_got - o.mean_avg_got AS difference
FROM patient_averages AS p
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o
WHERE o.mean_avg_got IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

b.request: For each patient with Laboratory records, show the patient ID, average GOT, average RBC, and the difference between their average GOT and the mean of all patients’ average GOT values. Compute averages while ignoring missing values; if the overall mean is missing, return no rows. Sort by the difference descending, placing missing differences last, return the top 10, and do not round
b.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(GOT) AS avg_got, AVG(RBC) AS avg_rbc
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
), overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_got) AS mean_avg_got
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT p.ID, p.avg_got, p.avg_rbc,
       p.avg_got - o.mean_avg_got AS difference
FROM patient_averages AS p
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS o
WHERE o.mean_avg_got IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

c.request: For each patient in `Laboratory`, show the patient ID, their average GOT, their average RBC, and their average GOT minus the overall average GOT. Use that one overall figure for every patient, and return nothing if it is missing. Ignore missing values. Sort by the difference, highest first with missing differences last, return the top 10, and don't round. Compare each patient's average GOT with the mean of the per-patient averages.
c.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(GOT) AS avg_got, AVG(RBC) AS avg_rbc
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
), overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_got) AS overall_avg_got
    FROM patient_averages
    WHERE avg_got IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT p.ID, p.avg_got, p.avg_rbc, p.avg_got - o.overall_avg_got AS got_difference
FROM patient_averages AS p
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o
ORDER BY got_difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

d.request: For each patient in `Laboratory`, show their ID, average GOT, average RBC, and the difference between their average GOT and the mean of all patients’ average GOT values. Ignore missing values, return nothing if the overall mean is missing, sort by the difference from highest to lowest with missing differences last, and return the top 10 without rounding.
d.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(GOT) AS avg_got, AVG(RBC) AS avg_rbc
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
), overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_got) AS mean_avg_got
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT p.ID, p.avg_got, p.avg_rbc,
       p.avg_got - o.mean_avg_got AS difference
FROM patient_averages AS p
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS o
WHERE o.mean_avg_got IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10
